Modern.brandNameRationale: Single syllable. Direct. A brim is the edge of a full cup, the moment before the first sip. The brand sits there. One word, easy to say, hard to forget.
Modern.industrySummary: Specialty coffee got crowded. Every neighborhood has one. The bar to feel different has gone up. People want speed, transparency, and a good cup. Not always in that order.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Blue Bottle (bluebottlecoffee.com) set the modern template. Counter Culture (counterculturecoffee.com) owns the wholesale wholesomeness. Onyx Coffee Lab (onyxcoffeelab.com) is who serious nerds buy from. Joe Coffee (joecoffeecompany.com) is what New York reaches for.
Modern.positioningStatement: The coffee for people who want the good cup in two minutes, not the lecture in twenty.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most third wave brands sell ritual. We sell a good cup fast. The opening is anyone who wants the quality without the slowness.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 40. Lives in a city. Works on a screen most of the day. Drinks coffee twice a day. Reads about food but doesn't post about it. Knows what an espresso costs. Picks the cafe with the shortest line and the best Wi-Fi.
behaviors: Orders the same drink for a year, then suddenly switches
Cares about beans but won't ask the barista
Has a strong opinion about oat milk

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. BRIM in a tight geometric sans. The M's right leg drops slightly below the baseline like the edge of a cup. Square icon for app and social uses a cup outline seen from the top with a thin ring inside marking the brim.

colorPalette.name: Stack Black
colorPalette.meaning: The color of dark roast in a white cup before milk hits it.

colorPalette.name: Bone
colorPalette.meaning: The paper cup. Used as space, not a hero.

colorPalette.name: Hot Orange
colorPalette.meaning: The accent. Used like a price tag, not a wall.

typography.primary: Custom geometric sans for the wordmark
typography.rationale: A clean grotesk reads fast on a small screen and looks modern on a chalkboard. We need both.

customSections.title: What it doesn't say
customSections.body: No crafted with care. No farm to cup. No founder photo holding beans. No tasting wheel.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: App first ordering. Cups are bone with a black sleeve. The shop has one chalkboard, rewritten by hand each morning, listing two coffees and three drinks. That is the whole menu.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words from different worlds. Amber for the color of a long pull. Tide for the slow arrival of the day. Sounds like a place you'd return to, not a place you'd discover.
Luxury.story: We started with one bag of Geisha beans, a borrowed grinder, and a stubborn idea. Coffee is a private hour, not a public performance. So we built a room where the kettle is the loudest thing.
Luxury.industrySummary: Coffee at the top end has been getting louder. Bigger glass, brighter signage, longer queues. There is room at the other end. Quieter rooms. Better cups. Fewer interruptions.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Sant Ambroeus (santambroeus.com) has the Milanese pedigree. Bar Pitti (barpitti.com) has the room. Maman (mamannyc.com) does the French country thing well. We are not loud and we are not casual. We are still.
Luxury.positioningStatement: The morning cup for people who guard their mornings.
Luxury.positioningRationale: There is an audience that has paid for everything and still wants more silence. They are not collecting cafes. They want one good one to return to.

targetAudience.primary: 35 to 60. Has money and uses it carefully. Travels, but always with the same hotel. Reads on paper. Walks in a coat that has seen ten winters. Doesn't like new things just because they are new.

dos: Name the bean. Name the room.
Speak like a host, not a salesperson

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark. Amber & Tide set in a high contrast classical face, with a small dotted divider between the two words. A monogram of the ampersand alone works for cups, gold foil for menus, blind embossed on paper.

colorPalette.name: Amber
colorPalette.meaning: The color of a long pour held to a window. Warm, not yellow.

colorPalette.name: Tide
colorPalette.meaning: Deep blue grey. The color of a cold harbor at five in the morning.

colorPalette.name: Bone China
colorPalette.meaning: The cup. Old paper. Cream walls.

colorPalette.name: Field

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and large type
typography.secondary: Söhne for body, menus, and digital
typography.rationale: A classical serif carries the room. The grotesk keeps the menu modern enough to read at distance.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No app ordering. No loyalty programs. No promotional signs. No latte art competitions. No music after 9 in the morning.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: The thing itself. French in origin, plain in English. A carafe is the vessel between the brewer and the cup. We named the brand after the middle, not the maker.
Minimal.industrySummary: Specialty coffee has more brands than the average person can name. Most of them work hard to feel different. There is an opening for one that doesn't.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Mast (mastbrothers.com) for design. Saint Frank (saintfrankcoffee.com) for restraint. Stumptown (stumptowncoffee.com) for the older quiet category leader. None of them are this quiet.
Minimal.positioningStatement: The coffee brand that doesn't try to be a brand.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who already know what they like. They buy one bag every two weeks. They do not need to be sold.

dos: Name the bean. Name the price.
donts: Add a story to a bag

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark. CARAFE in a single weight grotesk, set wide. No icon. No second mark. The wordmark works on a bag, a cup, and a window. That's the whole system.

colorPalette.name: Ink
colorPalette.meaning: The wordmark. The text. The line at the edge of the page.

typography.rationale: One typeface. One job. No mixing.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No flavor wheels. No origin stories on the bag. No founder photos. No social media campaigns. No QR codes.

Corporate.tagline: Coffee programs for the modern workplace.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Halton sounds like a place and a person at the same time. It reads as a real, older coffee firm. Coffee Co. closes it like a business. Easy on an invoice. Easy on the side of a van. Easy on a procurement spreadsheet.
Corporate.industrySummary: Office coffee used to mean a pot of stale roast on a hot plate. Companies now care about the cup their employees drink. The market has moved from cost center to part of the workplace experience.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Joe Coffee Office (joecoffeecompany.com) is the urban premium choice. Stumptown Wholesale (stumptowncoffee.com) carries credibility. Local roasters fight for the small accounts. Most are roasters first, service second. We are service first.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Better office coffee, run like a service, not a sale.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Procurement and office managers do not have time to source beans. They want one vendor, one invoice, one promise kept. We give them that, with coffee good enough that the team notices.

targetAudience.primary: Office managers, HR leads, facilities directors at companies of 50 to 5000 people. They sign the contract. They also catch the complaints.
motivations: Happy employees who stop complaining about the coffee

dos: Speak to the buyer, not the drinker

messagingPillars.name: One vendor
messagingPillars.description: Beans, machines, service, training. One contract. One contact.

messagingPillars.name: Predictable
messagingPillars.description: Fixed monthly billing. No surprise invoices. No equipment markups.

messagingPillars.name: Quality on the cup
messagingPillars.description: Specialty grade coffee, freshly roasted, calibrated machines, trained staff.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is an abstract sunrise, made of three horizontal lines stacked. Reads cleanly on a uniform, a van, and an email signature.

typography.rationale: Inter is widely supported and looks professional in every size. The serif gets reserved for printed quarterly business reviews.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No retail shops. No direct-to-consumer site. No flavored syrups. No seasonal logo redesigns. No celebrity partnerships.

Creative.brandNameRationale: A holler is a loud, friendly call. The Southern kind. The kind that means come over here, I want to tell you something. The brand name is also a verb. People should say it out loud.
Creative.manifesto: Coffee got serious. We respect that. But somewhere along the way we stopped having fun with it. The bag stopped having a personality. The cup stopped being something you smiled at. Holler is the brand that puts the joke back in your hand and the good coffee under it.
Creative.industrySummary: Most coffee brands speak in hushed tones. Earnest. Reverent. The room is full of brands trying to sound serious. There's room for one that is having a great time.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Sey (seycoffee.com) is the cool quiet one. Onyx Coffee Lab (onyxcoffeelab.com) is the nerd-prestige one. Devoción (devocion.com) has the lush warehouse thing. We're none of them. We're the loud friend at the table.
Creative.positioningStatement: Coffee that has a personality and isn't ashamed of it.

targetAudience.primary: 20s and 30s. Lives somewhere expressive. Buys art, makes art, or hangs out with people who do. Has opinions and shares them. Buys a bag of beans because the design made them laugh.

dos: Talk to one person, not the world
donts: Reach for sincerity that isn't there

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark with a megaphone built into the H. The H's left vertical stroke flares out into a horn shape. Used at large scale on bags and posters. A standalone megaphone mark works as a profile photo or sticker.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not minimal. Not quiet. Not earnest about beans. Not a manifesto-on-the-bag brand. Not afraid of cartoons.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Bags are illustrated. Each new release gets a different illustrator. The cafe has a wall of past bag art. Social is full of voice memos, behind the scenes, and the worst customer photos turned into the best stickers.
